tasks.short: Check stocks of grinding wheels, parts and tools on the shelves, record what is used, decide what to reorder, fill the reorder request, check it, send it to purchasing, and put deliveries away.

steps.what: Grinding machine operator checks stocks of machine parts and machining tools on the shelves: a full check today, spot checks after the change because scans keep stock current
Grinding machine operator records parts and tools used: on a paper list today; after the change by scanning the bin label of each item taken
Grinding machine operator decides which parts and tools to reorder
Grinding machine operator fills the reorder request by hand
Grinding machine operator checks the final reorder request: items, quantities, special wheels added by hand and that it goes to purchasing
Grinding machine operator releases the checked request to purchasing: handed over on paper today, by one release in the ERP after the change
Grinding machine operator puts delivered parts and tools away

tasks.design: Grinding wheels, dressing tools and spare parts get bin labels, and the operator scans each item taken in the ERP shop-floor module ({ERP}), so usage is not written on a paper list and stock levels stay current; shelf checks become spot checks. A reorder list shows items below their minimum level, and the requisition is built from the items the operator picks. The operator checks the final request and releases it once to purchasing in the system instead of walking it over on paper. Deciding what to reorder and putting deliveries away stay with the operator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Stock was checked by eye, usage written on paper and requests handed over on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: ERP shop-floor modules track stock by scan and build requisitions from minimum levels.
tasks.still_hard: Special wheels for one-off jobs have no minimum level.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing which wheel grade gives the right finish on a new material.
tasks.altitude: The operator decides on reorders instead of counting.

reach.learn: Whether requests arrive before stock runs out.

evidence.claim: Jay Industries reported 86% less inventory variance and 6% higher OEE with Plex MES; vendor case.
Scans tied to an operator login can observe performance and need works council consent.

assumptions: Boundary: from the shift start to stock replenished; supplier choice is outside.
Input contract: bins labelled and minimum levels set; fallback is the paper list.

The operator checks every request. Deciding, checking and putting away keep their full time. s1 keeps 50 because shelf checks become spot checks; s2 keeps 40 for scanning each item taken; s4 keeps 30 for picking items from the reorder list and adding special wheels; s6 keeps 10 for the release itself.
Works council consent comes before scans are tied to logins.
research_questions: Do machine stops for missing wheels fall?

incremental.description: Grinding machine operator corrects wrong or missed scans found in spot checks.

approvals.approved_version: The reorder request with items, quantities and needed dates exactly as checked by the operator in s5, released once to purchasing's requisition queue in {ERP}; any change needs a new check.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: many special wheels for one-off jobs and unlabelled bins, so about half of the items are still checked, written and requested by hand (19.7); high: bins labelled and minimum levels set as assumed (35.5).

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The grinding machine operator keeps deciding what to reorder and handling tools; eye checks, paper usage lists and paper requests shrink.
role.ambitious_version: An operator with more time at the machine.

job.title: Grinding, Lapping, Polishing, and Buffing Machine Tool Setters, Operators, and Tenders, Metal and Plastic
